newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Royal Dutch/Shell says optimistic on Gorgon.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Royal Dutch/Shell says optimistic on Gorgon.

text.p: The chief of the Royal Dutch/ Shell group said on Friday he was optimistic a deal could be reached to integrate the huge North West Shelf and Gorgon gas projects off northwest Australia.

Cor Herkstroter, chairman of the group's committee of managing directors, said plans for major expansion of the North West Shelf's liquified natural gas (LNG) capacity could not now be fully justified without integrating it with another project.

Asked if he was optimistic the owners of the North West Shelf project and the nearby Gorgon field could agree to develop the projects jointly, Herkstroter said: "If that is a viable option, which I think it is...I am inclined to think yes."
Royal Dutch/Shell is a part owner of each project.

The six North West Shelf partners are considering a A$5 billion proposal to double capacity at their 7.5 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) LNG plant on the Burrp Pensinsula, based on strong long-term demand from Japan.
But Herkstroter, who visited the North West Shelf project this week, told reporters in Melbourne more work needed to be done to justify such a major expansion in the North West Shelf.
"There's a difference between gas in place and gas that you can recover," he said.

"So you have to demonstrate to yourself that you can economically recover what there is in sufficiently large quantities that you can justify a project and you can indeed justify going out to customers and saying...rely on me."
"I think they (the North West Shelf) are coming close to it," Herstroter added.
Asked if expansion was justifiable now if gas from Gorgon was included in the North West Shelf, Herkstroter said: "It could be....If you had other projects in, then why not."
Royal Dutch/Shell, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, the MiMi consortium, Chevron Corp, British Petroleum Co and Woodside Petroleum each own a sixth of the North West Shelf.

Shell also owns two-sevenths of the Gorgon field, which has the capacity to produce 6 MTPA but is still subject to feasibility studies. The other partners are Chevron, Texaco Inc and Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd.
Shell and other main players in the two projects are under pressure from the Western Australia state government to decide soon on the future development of the state's LNG industry.

Shell Australia Ltd chief executive Roland Williams, who says it would be absurd to develop Gorgon as a stand-alone project with a greenfield LNG plant, said he believed an agreement to integrate the two projects was within reach.

"Our company occupies a rather central position: we are involved in both consortia and are also a major shareholder of the Woodside company (operator of the North West Shelf)," Williams told reporters on Friday.
"We are obviously aiming for an alignment between all the parties involved...and I believe we will get it."
The MiMi partner in the North West Shelf project is a 50-50 joint venture between Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp.
